items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: Same thing happened with Stan Getz he’d yes and no ya to death. So he had me close with the jazz.

ctx.x: they said, “Okay we want you, it’s your job, but Steve Allen had a nine piece orchestra, we’ll give you a nine piece orchestra.” I said, “I don’t want it.” They said, “Well what do you mean?” I said, “You mean they give me a big band because we’re opposite Johnny Carson? Or opposite Elliot Lawrence who was with Les Crane — those shows at that time they all had 16 piece bands. And to me a 16 piece band — give me a sextet. I said sextet? Can you make it with a sextet? You see working with Steve Allen, of course I…

in at Letter D, the ending.” Play the intro — the singer never knew we never played the middle. We’d never do it. So that’s what I learned. So I did that for my TV shows, and then, you know it was, it just came naturally to me because the harder part got later on. See all the talent we had for the first maybe two or three weeks, and that’s why Regis, in last, where all the talent that already were booked for Steve Allen. And Steve was a big jazz fan so he’d have Sarah Vaughan, Stan Getz, Oscar Peterson, Count…

items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So every time we had a jazz musician — Stan Getz, every time he interviewed, I had to be down there with him.

ctx.x: Well I got to know him, he was a fan of mine. [pause for refreshment] That’s right keep bringing ‘em in. Stop putting all that vodka in this. I quit drinking years ago. I thank you very much. He was a fan of mine. He used to come, in New York, when I played Birdland. He’d come in all the time to hear me. And when I moved out to California he’d come in to see me playing all the time. And I moved back to New York for almost a year and I got called, he was doing a television show and I got called — he quit the show…

a question, “yes,” “no,” he asked him. Finally I said, “Regis, I want to ask Basie a question.” He said, “Go ahead, Terry.” I went down and said, “Basie, when we played in Detroit that time, remember that scene with Pee Wee Marquette? Tell Regis.” He had to tell the story now. So every time we had a jazz musician — Stan Getz, every time he interviewed, I had to be down there with him. He was really great. That wasn’t his bag. I used to put him on all the time. He always thought that we were putting him on because…
